sections.text:
8 = Plut, 28, cod. 14. — Chartac. cm. 19,8 × 15, ff. 321 (nonnulla ex integro vel
partim vacua) s. XIV exeuntis [cf. capp. κεʹ et υιςʹ]. Pristina numeratio : quaternio-
nes α — μ; desunt quaterniones duo ante καʹ. Codicem exaraverunt variae manus:
1a ff. 1 — 4 + 9 + 310 — 314; 2a ff. 4v — 8 + 9v + 10v + 17 (quae ad carmen
spectant) + 315v — 321; 3a ff. 10 + 11 + 17 usque ad carmen + 18 — 309. F. 1
sections.en: 8 = Plut, 28, cod. 14. — Paper, 19.8 × 15 cm, 321 folios (some entirely or partly empty) from the end of the 14th century [cf. chapters 25 and 416]. Original numbering: quires 1 — 40; two quires are missing before 21. Various hands wrote the codex: 1st ff. 1 — 4 + 9 + 310 — 314; 2nd ff. 4v — 8 + 9v + 10v + 17 (which relate to the poem) + 315v — 321; 3rd ff. 10 + 11 + 17 up to the poem + 18 — 309. F. 1

sections.text:
1 Opusculum est ψευδεπίγραφον circa ann. 775 p. C. n. compositum; vide Usener,
Index Schol. Bonn., 1879, p. 9 sqq. Idem edidit in ind. schol. anni 1880.
sections.en: 1 The short work is pseudepigraphic (ψευδεπίγραφον), composed around the year 775 A.D.; see Usener, Index Schol. Bonn., 1879, p. 9 sqq. The same man edited it in the index schol. of the year 1880.

summary.headline: Astrological Medicine and Prognosis
summary.text: Catalog of Florentine codex folios 233–240, listing astrological medical texts on phlebotomy, purgation, diseases, physicians, decumbitures, diagnosis, prognosis, surgery, and averting rituals. It identifies works by Pankarios, Hephaistion, and Stephanos of Alexandria, including Stephanos’s treatise addressed to Timotheos and prompted by Muhammad’s legislation.
